prerequisites: It is recommended to take Fluid Mechanics I/Introduction to Fluid Mechanics concurrently

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.

syllabus_topics: Principles of Thermodynamics. Temperature, internal energy and entropy.
Evaluation of properties of pure substances. Simplified substance models (ideal gas and incompressible substance). Equations of state.
Balances of matter, energy, entropy and exergy in non-reactive open and closed systems.
Energy and the first law of Thermodynamics.
Properties of a pure, simple and compressible substance.
Energy analysis in a control volume.
Non-reactive mixtures of ideal gases and psychrometry.
teaching_methods: Use of ICT (Information and Communication Technologies)
Audiovisual material in the virtual course
Comprehensive and detailed reading of course content supplemented with base text chapters
Elaboration of conceptual and synoptic schemes

assessment_methods.method: Continuous Assessment Tests (Pruebas de Evaluación Continua - PEC)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must obtain at least 5 out of 10 in the presential exam (PP) and a "Pass" grade in the laboratory practices (LAB). The final grade is obtained according to the algorithm: `NOTA=MIN(10 ; 0.9 * PP + 0.1 * average_PECs + 0.1 * LAB)` if both conditions are met. Otherwise, the grade is "Fail". A minimum of 1.0 points is required in each block (questions and problems) of the presential exam. Continuous assessment tests (PECs) and lab practices contribute additional points to the final score, with the final grade capped at 10.
